-C.help: Colorize matches in packet contents output.

-D.help: When reading pcap_dump files, replay them at their recorded time intervals (mimic realtime).

-N.help: Show sub-protocol number along with single-character identifier (useful when observing raw or unknown protocols).

-R.help: Do not try to drop privileges to the DROPPRIVS_USER (specified at build-time). ngrep makes no effort to validate input from live or offline sources as it is focused more on performance and handling large amounts of data than protocol correctness, which is most often a fair assumption to make.  However, sometimes it matters and thus as a rule ngrep will try to be defensive and drop any root privileges it might have. There exist scenarios where this behaviour can become an obstacle, so this option is provided to end-users who want to disable this feature, but must do so with an understanding of the risks.  Packets can be randomly malformed or even specifically designed to overflow sniffers and take control of them, and revoking root privileges is currently the only risk mitigation ngrep employs against such an attack.  Use this option and turn it off at your own risk.

-T.help: Print a timestamp in the form of +S.UUUUUU, indicating the delta between packet matches.  Specify a second time to indicate the delta since the first packet match.

-U.help: Display UTF-8 characters in packet contents output.

-X.help: Treat the match expression as a hexadecimal string.  See the explanation of match expression below.

-e.help: Show empty packets.  Normally empty packets are discarded because they have no payload to search.  If specified, empty packets will be shown, regardless of the specified regex expression.

-i.help: Ignore case for the regex expression.

-p.help: Don't put the interface into promiscuous mode.

-q.help: Be quiet; don't output any information other than packet headers and their payloads (if relevant).

-r.help: Resolve container IP addresses to their Docker or Podman container names. When enabled, IP addresses are displayed as in packet output.  If the Docker or Podman socket is accessible, ngrep uses the Events API for real-time container tracking.  Otherwise, it falls back to CLI-based polling with a 30-second cache TTL.  This feature can be excluded at build time with

-t.help: Print a timestamp in the form of YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS.UUUUUU everytime a packet is matched.

-u.help: Display UTF-8 characters in packet contents output.

-v.help: Invert the match; only display packets that don't match.

-w.help: Match the regex expression as a word.

-x.help: Dump packet contents as both hexadecimal and ASCII.
